findings.summary: The CI history check walks every commit in merge_base..tip, so a resync merge that brings in other governed content would fail every later pull request permanently.
findings.evidence: check_after_cutover lists `rev-list --reverse merge_base..tip` and runs classify_pre_merge on each commit with no exclusion. CI runs `athena check --history` on pull requests (ci.yml:606). Under the plan, resync merges and squashed landing commits are never reachable from main, so they stay in every later PR head's own commits. The plan's risk says only that the check 'could report it' and leaves it as a user question; nothing tests it. A senior engineer would not ship a design in which one hand-landed change on main makes every future PR fail a required check with no fix short of a rewrite. Fix: Give the gate one rule, in athena-gate so core and the history check share it. Either (a) treat a merge as covered when its second parent is an ancestor of main and its tree equals merge_tree(landed, first parent, second parent), so everything it adds beyond its first parent came from main, which attribution already covers; or (b) apply the same landed-head exclusion inside history.rs. Use the rule in pr_commits, check_pr_head and check_after_cutover, and add a test where main moved by other governed content before the resync.
findings.location: Dependents: 'History check on a head that holds a resync merge'; crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs:142-153; .github/workflows/ci.yml:606

findings.summary: Which commits are excluded from the governance classification is decided by a free-text line in a commit message, against the code's own 'messages are never read' rule, even though authoritative data already exists.
findings.evidence: The pr_commits doc (land.rs:245-246) says 'each classified from its content alone. Messages are never read', and classify_pre_merge's doc (invariant.rs:311) says the same. pr_range would drop `^landed` and all of its ancestors because of a message line, so a hand-written or mistaken line hides arbitrary commits from the landing intent, the landing record and `check --pr-head`. Landing records already store the PR head and the host commit (athena-data/src/history.rs:228-230, `head_sha`, `host_commit`), and CI fetches athena/records (ci.yml:548). Fix: Derive the exclusion from landing records: exclude the head_sha (and its ancestors) of every landing whose host_commit is an ancestor of the remote base. If the message line stays as a hint, verify it before use: the merge's second parent is on main, the named commit is an ancestor of the first parent, and the merge tree equals merge_tree(landed, p1, p2). Add a test where a forged line on a hand merge excludes nothing.
findings.location: Change 3 / Decision 2 / Step 3: pr_range keyed on the `Resynced-Landed` message line

findings.summary: The drain push test may pass without the push, because nothing guarantees the branch head moves between landings.
findings.evidence: The probe 'returns Landed as RecordingLander does'. RecordingLander (tests/drain.rs:2291-2300) makes no commit, so the branch head may stay at the commit pushed during setup. The assertions 'remote tip equals the local head after the first landing' and 'after the drain the remote tip equals the final local head' then hold without any push, contradicting the plan's 'Fails without the behavior' claim. Fix: Have the probe lander make a commit on the branch before returning Landed, as ConfigLander does (tests/drain.rs:3371-3378). Assert that the local head after each landing differs from the remote tip recorded before that landing, then that the remote tip equals it at the next landing and at the end.

findings.summary: The plan doesn't state that under append-only the PR range (origin/main..head) grows with every landing forever.
findings.evidence: Squashed commits never become reachable from main, so each landing adds its commits and a resync merge to every later head's own commits. The CI history check (history.rs:143-153) classifies all of them on every PR, and the host's PR commit list grows with them. Only plan_rebase is named as a risk. Fix: State the growth, its effect on CI history-check time, and that per-job branches (D167) are the long-term answer; or make the shared range rule from finding 1 bound the walk by excluding landed heads in the history check as well.

summary: The plan targets the real root cause (resync_tip's git.replay at land.rs:228) and its core mechanism is sound: merge_tree with the landed commit as base, commit_tree with parents [head, merged], reset_keep, and a plain push_branch. All the Git APIs it names exist (merge_tree with explicit merge base, commit_tree, reset_keep, push_branch, GitRemote::remote_head), and so do the line references. Keeping already-squashed commits in the branch, though, changes what every later pull-request head contains, and the plan handles that only partly. (1) CI's required `athena check --history` (ci.yml:606) classifies every commit in merge_base..tip with no exclusion (athena-gate/src/history.rs:142-153). A resync merge that carries main content beyond the landed job would fail that check on every later pull request forever, because the merge never reaches main. The plan leaves this as a user question with no test. (2) The new pr_range decides which commits escape classification from a commit-message line. pr_commits and classify_pre_merge both document that messages are never read, and landing records already name each landed PR head and host commit, which is authoritative data. (3) The drain demonstration may pass without the push, because the probe lander (like RecordingLander) makes no commit, so the remote tip can equal the local head without any push. Smaller points: a doc comment at test_support.rs:616 is missed, and the plan doesn't state the unbounded growth of the PR range under append-only. I did not repeat Athena's scope findings; the extra files look justified.
